### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-email`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via EmailServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via EmailServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fb7f2f6a31c1e3d327f1c87b82d026b22b5dd0ae` — the merge of head `63bafb1a987316ea2f51a12389c263f17f31b5e6` into base `7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fb7f2f6a31c1e3d327f1c87b82d026b22b5dd0ae && git checkout fb7f2f6a31c1e3d327f1c87b82d026b22b5dd0ae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca 63bafb1a987316ea2f51a12389c263f17f31b5e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca && git merge --no-ff 63bafb1a987316ea2f51a12389c263f17f31b5e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7e8b31ce5d96a35ac9b45d9aa30f637ad3495eca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT at `Head-sha: 63bafb1a987316ea2f51a12389c263f17f31b5e6` (2026-11-10T11:48Z).

- **Shape:** a no-card order from the security#1 seat, in two rounds. A contract-tier reviewer approved the order with seven edits before dispatch. Round 2 applied the PR review's edits: an admitted connection must carry the host's socket, two more `transportOptions` keys are refused, and the README sample is corrected. 11 files, +831 / −14. Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 32175`: 0 of 11 paths). `Clause-②: yes` (an additive host option and exported types) · `Metadata-protocol: none` · `patch`. No `!`, and the default is unchanged.
- **Ruling:** the maintainer's 「框架立卡 高优先级」 (2026-11-10): a framework host seam, with no change to the framework default.
- **Premise measured:**
  - With the option set, every SMTP transport the plugin builds (boot, saved settings, `mail/test`) asks the host's policy for each connection. The policy is applied last. A socket-less answer fails the connection. Keys that would select another connection or transport kind are refused at construction.
  - Without the option, all three sites hand nodemailer today's options; the CONTROL literals were re-proven against the base source.
  - Ablations: seven, each red, each restored. A census test pins that no fourth construction site skips the seam.
- **Gates:**
  - CI on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, nothing else.
  - Locally: 68 derived families; 66 exit 0. The other 2 are NOT MEASURED (they need every package's dist) and are covered by CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`, which is `success`.
  - No dogfood battery is owed: no `!` and no narrowing arm.
- **Review:** the isolated contract-tier reviewer returned APPROVE-WITH-EDITS on the first head, then PASS on this head. Its one wording nit on the body is applied by the seat.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - The option is documented in the package README, because no `content/docs` page documents the plugin's constructor options.
  - The fake SMTP testkit gained a read-only connection counter.
  - The dev's open question was decided by the seat as option B, on the reviewer's recommendation, while the type is unreleased.
- **Landing:** the seat lands it through the merge queue (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`).

Implemented-by: os-dev (security#1 order, `session_017xRBcT1w3zpekijraHJE4f`) · Reviewed-by: isolated contract-tier reviewers (the order, then the PR, then a same-head confirmation).

**Queue dequeue, read and re-queued once.** The merge queue dropped this PR on `CI_FAILURE`: `Dogfood Regression Gate`, because shard `dogfood-3-of-3` hit the 30-minute job timeout in queue group `5da3c209f6` (check run 129840653460). No test failed; the leg was cancelled mid-run, and its log is no longer retrievable.

It reads as not this PR's:
- The same head `63bafb1a98` passed the whole queue CI in the earlier group `c53d7f645b`.
- In the ten other queue groups started at the same minute, `dogfood-3-of-3` finished in 12–17 minutes.
- The diff touches only `@objectstack/plugin-email`, and with no host option it hands nodemailer today's options byte for byte (pinned).

Re-queued once (`automerge_enable`). If the same shard fails again, the seat treats it as real and measures the battery locally on this head.
